messages:
alex_support: FYI Acme Analytics reporting their ingest webhook started returning 403 for our private/VPC traffic around 09:10 PT. Customer says nothing changed on their side.

acme_sre: yep started at 09:08, see spike of 403s in our logs. We didn't deploy anything. Blocking URL is https://events.acme-analytics.com/hook/rdw

alex_support: Repro steps I'm running now from the customer-dedicated VPC (private deployment env). Will paste outputs.

sam_ops: tagging infra, could be SNAT/egress rotation. I saw a small NAT rebalance earlier this morning.

alex_support: curl -v from private-instance -> shows 403:
```
> curl -i -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"x":1}' https://events.acme-analytics.com/hook/rdw
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:11:02 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "IP not allowlisted" }
```

alex_support: check our outbound IP from that host:
```
> curl -s https://ifconfig.me
3.210.45.67
```

alex_support: customer allowlist (from earlier case notes) contains 3.198.45.67 and 3.198.45.68, not the IP above.

jon_infra: infra-bot shows SNAT pool reassign at 09:04 for the private cluster due to capacity rebalancing. deploy-bot log: `snat-pool/cluster-a -> pool-b (elastic-ips: 3.210.45.66-3.210.45.70)`

infra-bot: Maintenance note: automated SNAT reassign executed by reclaim-controller at 2026-03-15T09:04:06Z for cluster-a. Old pool (3.198.45.66-3.198.45.70) released.

acme_sre: so our requests are coming from a new EIP range. We allowlist IPs, not hostnames. Can we confirm what IPs were used in the window?

jon_infra: checking NAT logs, here's connection sample around 09:10:
```
src=10.2.8.21 dst=events.acme-analytics.com dnat=34.56.78.90 snat=3.210.45.67
src=10.2.8.22 dst=events.acme-analytics.com dnat=34.56.78.90 snat=3.210.45.68
```

alex_support: forwarded to Acme SRE: you need to add 3.210.45.66-3.210.45.70 to your allowlist. I've included the ticket link.

acme_sre: can you hold on modifications? Our infra team only accepts CIDR ranges from our security team and they need an RFC. Also, does Redwood provide a stable hostname we can allowlist instead?

sam_ops: short-term: we can temporarily rebind an IP from the old pool to ensure continuity while they update. Long-term: recommend allowing via the egress-hostname (egress.acme.redwood.com) which we maintain with DNS pointing to the current SNAT EIPs; but DNS-based allowlisting has limitations if they resolve to single IPs and then firewall does reverse-checks.

jon_infra: action item: allocate a floating EIP to preserve at least one outgoing address for this customer's VPC for 24h. Creating request now.

deploy-bot: EIP allocation in progress (req-4852). ETA ~5 mins.

jon_infra: allocated 3.198.45.69 and bound it to the SNAT gateway for cluster-a as a sticky alias for Acme for 24h. This should match an IP already in their allowlist (3.198.45.66-70 range).

alex_support: Acme SRE can you retest now?

acme_sre: retesting...

acme_sre: confirmed -- retries show 200s now. Thank you. We will update our firewall rules to include 3.210.45.66-3.210.45.70 but will coordinate with our security team for CIDR approvals (may take a day).

alex_support: Good. Next steps: 1) keep the sticky EIP bound for 24h (jon) 2) share the full list of new EIPs and ranges (sam) 3) recommend customer change to domain-based allowlisting or use our published egress CIDR set (support doc: https://redwood.example.com/docs/egress-ip-ranges) 4) create follow-up ticket for Dedicated customers to request persistent EIPs as part of config.

sam_ops: I'll email networking the ranges and add a note to the case: new EIPs 3.210.45.66-3.210.45.70. Also attaching repro logs and curl snippets.

acme_sre: one ask — can Redwood provide an HMAC header we sign so customer can authenticate requests independent of source IP? That would remove allowlist fragility.

alex_support: yes, we have webhook signing (docs linked). I'll enable signing on their customer config and rotate keys with them next week.

jon_infra: setting sticky EIP TTL: 24h. I'll add infra postmortem note: SNAT reassign is allowed but we should notify support for clusters with active webhook customers. Adding a preemptive message to the change log.

infra-bot: Note added to change-log: `snat-rebalance` notification to #support added.

alex_support: marking thread resolved once customer confirms allowlist update in their firewall. Closing condition: customer updates to add new EIP range or we provision permanent EIPs.

acme_sre: will update once security team approves. Thanks all :tada:

alex_support: resolved -> temporary sticky EIP applied, customer requests webhook signing enabled, action items opened: TICKET-9823 (permanent EIP request), TICKET-9824 (enable webhook signing), TICKET-9825 (docs update re: DNS vs IP allowlisting).
